note: Single source of truth. Edit this file to add recipes. See README for the compact ingredient syntax.

chicken.label: chicken
chicken.cook: Grill over direct medium heat, 6–7 minutes a side, to 175°F internal. Thighs want to go past 165°F — that is where they turn tender.
chicken.reheat: Warm the sliced chicken in a covered skillet with a splash of water or broth. The steam is what keeps it from drying out.
chicken.prep: Pat dry and season at least 20 minutes ahead.

turkey.label: ground turkey
turkey.cook: Brown in a heavy pot in batches. Let it sit undisturbed to build a crust before breaking it up.
turkey.reheat: Warm gently with a splash of water — it dries out fast.
turkey.prep: Buy plain ground turkey, not seasoned patties.

salmon.label: salmon
salmon.cook: Roast skin-down at 400°F for 12–14 minutes. Pull it while the center is still slightly translucent.
salmon.reheat: Do not. Flake it cold into the dish and let residual heat warm it through.
salmon.prep: Salt 30 minutes ahead and leave uncovered in the fridge.

whitefish.label: white fish
whitefish.cook: Roast at 400°F for 10–12 minutes until it flakes under light pressure.
whitefish.reheat: Serve cold and flaked, or warm very gently in a covered pan.
whitefish.prep: Pat very dry — wet fish steams instead of browning.

swordfish.label: swordfish
swordfish.cook: Grill over direct high heat about 4 minutes a side. It overcooks fast — pull it the moment it flakes but still holds together.
swordfish.reheat: Serve cold and flaked. Reheating turns it tough.
swordfish.prep: Oil the steaks, not the grate.

shrimp.label: shrimp
shrimp.cook: Grill over high heat 2 minutes a side. Done the moment they curl into a C — a tight O means overcooked.
shrimp.reheat: Poorly. Cook shrimp fresh the night you eat it.
shrimp.prep: Buy plain — pre-marinated shrimp is almost always garlic-forward.

tofu.label: tofu
tofu.cook: Press 45 minutes, cube, toss in cornstarch, air fry at 400°F for 14 minutes, shaking halfway.
tofu.reheat: Air fry 5 minutes at 375°F to bring the crust back.
tofu.prep: Press it Sunday and leave it in marinade — it needs no cooking until you want it.

beans.label: white beans
beans.cook: Simmer with the aromatics 15 minutes, mashing some against the pot to thicken.
beans.reheat: Warm with a splash of water; they thicken overnight.
beans.prep: Rinse well. Skip anything labeled seasoned or chili-style.

eggs.label: eggs
eggs.cook: Jammy-boil 7 minutes, then ice bath. They keep peeled for four days.

artichoke.label: artichoke hearts
artichoke.cook: Halve, pat very dry, bread, and bake at 425°F for 20 minutes until browned and crisp.
artichoke.reheat: Air fry 5 minutes at 375°F. They lose their crunch fast, so bread them Sunday and bake the night you eat them.
artichoke.prep: Drain and dry thoroughly — wet artichokes will not take breading.

chickpeas.label: chickpeas
chickpeas.cook: Dry well, toss with oil and smoked paprika, roast at 425°F for 25 minutes until they rattle.
chickpeas.reheat: Air fry 4 minutes at 375°F to bring back the crunch.
chickpeas.prep: Rinse and dry on a towel. Skip seasoned varieties.

beef.label: beef
beef.cook: Grill over high heat 4–5 minutes a side for medium-rare, then rest 10 minutes before slicing against the grain.
beef.reheat: Warm gently, covered, with a splash of broth — red meat overcooks fast on a second pass.
beef.prep: Salt at least 40 minutes ahead, or overnight, and bring to room temperature before it hits the grill.
beef.accommodateNote: Grill or sear a portion of chicken thighs or salmon alongside with the same rub, for your spouse's plate — same timing as the household default, different protein.

pork.label: pork
pork.cook: Tenderloin: grill or roast to 140–145°F, about 20 minutes. Shoulder: smoke low and slow to 195°F for pulling.
pork.reheat: Warm with a splash of liquid, covered — pork dries out fast reheated uncovered.
pork.prep: Trim the silver skin off tenderloin before cooking.
pork.accommodateNote: Cook a portion of chicken thighs the same way for your spouse — same rub, same pan or smoker, pulled a bit earlier since poultry cooks faster.

groundbeef.label: ground beef
groundbeef.cook: Brown in a hot pan in batches, breaking it up once it's developed a crust, not before.
groundbeef.reheat: Warm gently with a splash of water or sauce.
groundbeef.prep: Don't crowd the pan or it steams instead of browning.
groundbeef.accommodateNote: Brown a half-pound of ground turkey separately, same seasoning, same pan — it's a small enough batch to cook alongside without extra dishes.

rice.label: rice
rice.cook: Rice cooker, double batch. Spread on a sheet pan to cool before storing.
rice.reheat: Add a tablespoon of water per cup and cover.

tortilla.label: corn tortillas
tortilla.reheat: 20 seconds a side in a dry skillet.

potato.label: potatoes
potato.cook: Boil until fork-tender, smash on an oiled sheet pan, roast at 450°F for 35 minutes.
potato.reheat: Air fryer, 400°F for 6 minutes. They come back almost new.

sweetpotato.label: sweet potatoes
sweetpotato.cook: Bake whole at 400°F for 50 minutes until collapsing.
sweetpotato.reheat: Air fryer, 380°F for 8 minutes — the skin re-crisps.

pasta.label: GF pasta
pasta.cook: Boil to just under package time, drain, rinse cold, toss with oil.
pasta.reheat: Warm directly in sauce with a splash of pasta water.
pasta.accommodateNote: Boil a small separate pot of GF penne or spaghetti for your spouse — a cup dry is plenty for one serving. Keep it in its own pot; GF pasta clouds the water fast.

farro.label: farro
farro.cook: Simmer 1 cup dry farro in salted water 25-30 minutes until tender but chewy, drain.
farro.reheat: Warm with a splash of water, covered.
farro.accommodateNote: Cook a small pot of quinoa alongside for your spouse instead of farro — about 1 cup dry, ready in 15 minutes, same salt water.

quinoa.label: quinoa
quinoa.cook: Rinse, then simmer 1 part quinoa to 2 parts water, covered, 15 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
quinoa.reheat: Warm with a splash of water, covered.

lasagna.label: lasagna noodles
lasagna.cook: Boil in heavily salted water to al dente per package time — don't overcook or they'll tear when rolled.
lasagna.reheat: n/a — baked once, eaten from the dish.
lasagna.accommodateNote: Boil 2-3 GF lasagna noodles separately for your spouse's roll-ups — they turn to mush fast if boiled together with regular.

millet.label: millet
millet.cook: Toast dry in a pot 2 minutes, then simmer 1 part millet to 2.5 parts water, covered, 18-20 minutes until fluffy.
millet.reheat: Warm with a splash of water, covered.

produce.note: Seasonal produce guide adapted from Love & Lemons. Alliums removed to match household rules. Availability varies by region.

components.name: Allium-free BBQ sauce
components.why: Every bottled BBQ sauce has onion or garlic powder, and many thicken with wheat.
steps: Sweat the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes until soft, then add garlic for 30 seconds.
Add tomato paste, cider vinegar, molasses, Dijon, and smoked paprika with 1 cup water.
Simmer 20 minutes until it coats a spoon.
components.accommodate: Pull a cup of the sauce right after the tomato paste goes in, before the onion and garlic have simmered into it — or just simmer your spouse's cup separately with a little extra vinegar and paprika to fill the gap.

components.name: Allium-free chicken broth
components.why: Onion and garlic are back in as the base aromatics — this is a normal stock now.
ingredients: 3 lb chicken wings or saved carcasses
steps: Cover everything with 4 quarts cold water in a big pot.
Bring to a bare simmer — never a boil — and hold it there 3 hours.
Strain, salt to taste, cool, and freeze what you won't use in five days.
components.accommodate: Ladle out 2 quarts before the onion and garlic go in and simmer that portion separately with just the carrot, celery, and herbs — that's your spouse's stock for the week.

components.name: Cashew Caesar dressing
components.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Grilled Romaine Vegan Caesar Wedges
components.why: This is the original garlicky cashew Caesar. The capers and Dijon are still doubled up from before, so it stays bright even alongside the garlic.
steps: Soak the cashews in boiling water for 10 minutes if your blender isn't high-powered. Drain.
Blend cashews with the garlic clove, 1/2 cup water, 2 Tbsp lemon juice, capers, Dijon, nutritional yeast, salt, and a lot of black pepper.
Run it until genuinely creamy — a full minute.
It thickens overnight. Loosen with water each time you use it.
components.accommodate: Blend your spouse's portion first, before the garlic clove goes in, then blend the rest of the batch with garlic added. Two short blends instead of one.

components.name: Smoked paprika chimichurri
components.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Chimichurri Potato Salad
components.why: Chimichurri is normally minced garlic and scallion. Smoked paprika, oregano, and a hard hit of vinegar carry it instead — the smoke does the heavy lifting.
steps: Finely chop about a half cup of parsley, reserving a spoonful for garnish later in the week.
Whisk with olive oil, vinegar, minced garlic, smoked paprika, oregano, red pepper flakes, and a half teaspoon of salt.
Let it sit at least 20 minutes — it sharpens considerably as it stands.
Doubles as a marinade for grilled protein and a drizzle for roasted vegetables.
components.accommodate: Whisk a small side jar without the garlic, using a bit more vinegar and parsley to keep it from tasting flat — your spouse's portion.

components.name: Creamy avocado-dill dressing
components.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Gem Salad with Creamy Dill Dressing
components.why: The original blends in a garlic clove. Extra lemon and a pinch of celery seed cover the gap.
steps: Blend the avocado with the garlic clove, 3 Tbsp lemon juice, a quarter cup of chopped dill, 1/2 cup water, celery seed, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Run until completely smooth, adding water a splash at a time.
This one browns — make it last in the session and press plastic wrap directly onto the surface.
components.accommodate: Blend a small batch without the garlic first and set it aside for your spouse, then add garlic to the rest.

components.name: Herb-caper yogurt
components.why: Capers and lemon supply the sharpness a raw shallot would.
steps: Grate the cucumber and squeeze it dry in a towel — skip this and the sauce waters out by Tuesday.
Stir into yogurt with chopped dill, minced chives, chopped capers, lemon zest and juice, salt, and pepper.
components.accommodate: Mix your spouse's portion before the chives go in — dill and capers carry it fine without.

components.name: Maple-Dijon vinaigrette
components.why: Dijon and vinegar cover the sharp note a shallot would carry.
steps: Shake everything in a jar with salt, pepper, and thyme.
Re-shake before each use.

components.name: Fennel marinara
components.why: Back to a normal soffritto-style marinara — onion and garlic sweated properly instead of worked around.
steps: Sweat the diced onion in olive oil with salt for 8 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more, just until fragrant — don't let it brown.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and a pinch of chili. Simmer 30 minutes uncovered.
components.accommodate: Set aside 2 cups of crushed tomatoes before the onion and garlic go in. Simmer that portion on its own with just oregano and a little extra olive oil — it's flatter, so finish it with a splash of vinegar and more salt for your spouse.

components.name: Peanut-lime sauce
components.why: Doubles as a dressing, a dipping sauce, and a noodle sauce.
steps: Whisk everything with hot water until it pours.
It thickens hard in the fridge — loosen with hot water each night.
components.accommodate: Whisk a small side portion using tamari instead of soy sauce for your spouse — same ratios, same jar otherwise.

components.name: Quick-pickled vegetables
components.why: Ten minutes of work that makes every reheated bowl taste deliberate.
steps: Shave everything thin on a mandoline or peeler.
Cover with rice vinegar, a spoon of honey, and a big pinch of salt.
Ready in 30 minutes, better on day three.

components.name: Roasted vegetable tray
components.why: The vegetable side for all three nights, made once.
steps: Cut everything to roughly the same size and spread across two sheet pans — crowding steams instead of roasting.
Oil, salt, thyme, 425°F for 40–45 minutes until the edges genuinely darken.
Re-crisp any night in the air fryer at 400°F for 6 minutes.

components.name: Roasted salsa verde
components.why: Jarred salsa verde is always onion-based. Roasting your own takes 30 minutes and makes enough for three meals.
steps: Halve the tomatillos, stem the peppers, quarter the onion, spread on a sheet pan with the garlic wrapped in foil. Oil and salt everything.
Roast at 450°F for 25 minutes until the vegetables are blistered and slack.
Blend most of the tray with cilantro, lime juice, cumin, and salt — hold back a portion of the roasted tomatillo and poblano before blending in the onion and garlic.
Simmer 20 minutes to knock off the raw edge.
components.accommodate: Blend your spouse's portion from the reserved tomatillo and poblano only, with extra lime and cilantro to compensate for the missing onion and garlic.

components.name: Cabbage-lime slaw
components.why: The crunch and acid that make reheated food taste like a fresh meal.
steps: Shred the cabbage and carrots.
Salt the cabbage 20 minutes and squeeze it dry, or it waters out.
Toss with lime, vinegar, celery seed, honey, and salt.
Dress only half now — keep the rest undressed so it stays crisp all week.

components.name: Sheet pan squash soup
components.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Sheet Pan Squash Soup
components.why: This is the original recipe's method — a whole roasted onion and five cloves of garlic blended right into the base.
steps: Halve the squash lengthwise and scrape the seeds out. Cut the onion into quarters.
Squash and onion cut-side down on a parchment-lined sheet pan, drizzled with a tablespoon of oil, salt, and pepper. Wrap the garlic in foil and add it to the pan.
Roast at 400°F for 40–50 minutes, until the squash gives easily and the onion is nicely browned.
Scoop the squash flesh into a blender with the roasted onion, peeled garlic, broth, miso, vinegar, and the remaining oil. Blend about a minute until fully creamy.
Season aggressively — squash soup takes more salt than you expect.
components.accommodate: Before blending, set aside a cup of the roasted squash on its own. Blend it with a splash of broth and a little extra miso for your spouse — no onion, no garlic, still creamy.

components.name: Greek yogurt tartar sauce
components.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Greek Yogurt Tartar Sauce
components.why: Standard tartar sauce is built on minced shallot. Capers and lemon zest do it without.
steps: Stir yogurt with chopped capers, minced shallot, Dijon, lemon zest and juice, chopped dill, salt, and pepper.
Let it sit 15 minutes before tasting.
components.accommodate: Stir your spouse's portion together before the shallot goes in — capers and lemon carry it fine alone.

components.name: Date ball base
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, title unconfirmed), adapted — spot-check quantities against the book
components.why: One base, six flavors. The base is always the same 10 dates and a pinch of salt — the food processor does the rest.
steps: Pulse the dates and salt in a food processor until they form a sticky, crumbly mass.
This is the base every flavor below builds on — don't add mix-ins yet, that happens per flavor.

components.name: Lemon tahini dressing
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, p.219, title unconfirmed), adapted
components.why: The dressing that makes the farro and sweet potato taste like one dish instead of two sides.
steps: Whisk tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt.
Add water a tablespoon at a time, whisking, until it's pourable — tahini seizes up before it loosens, keep whisking through that stage.
Thin further with water each time you use it; it firms up in the fridge.
components.accommodate: Whisk a small batch without the garlic clove for your spouse — lemon carries it fine alone.

components.name: Cucumber dill pickles
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Homemade Pickles: One Brine, Four Ways'), adapted
components.why: One brine, four jars. Make all four the same afternoon and you've got condiments for weeks.
steps: Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Pack the vegetables and aromatics into a 16-ounce jar.
Pour the hot brine over, let cool, then chill overnight before eating.
This one brine recipe makes enough for two jars — double it if you're packing all four at once.
components.accommodate: Pack a third small jar without garlic for your spouse — same brine, same everything else.

components.name: Yellow squash pickles
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Homemade Pickles: One Brine, Four Ways'), adapted
components.why: One brine, four jars. Make all four the same afternoon and you've got condiments for weeks.
steps: Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Pack the vegetables and aromatics into a 16-ounce jar.
Pour the hot brine over, let cool, then chill overnight before eating.
This one brine recipe makes enough for two jars — double it if you're packing all four at once.
components.accommodate: Pack a third small jar without garlic for your spouse.

components.name: Quick pickled red onions
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Homemade Pickles: One Brine, Four Ways'), adapted
components.why: One brine, four jars. Make all four the same afternoon and you've got condiments for weeks.
steps: Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Pack the vegetables and aromatics into a 16-ounce jar.
Pour the hot brine over, let cool, then chill overnight before eating.
This one brine recipe makes enough for two jars — double it if you're packing all four at once.
components.accommodate: This one is onion by definition — there's no version of it for your spouse. Use the cucumber-dill or cauliflower jar for her plate instead when this is the topping.

components.name: Cauliflower pickles
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Homemade Pickles: One Brine, Four Ways'), adapted
components.why: One brine, four jars. Make all four the same afternoon and you've got condiments for weeks.
steps: Heat the vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a saucepan until the sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Pack the vegetables and aromatics into a 16-ounce jar.
Pour the hot brine over, let cool, then chill overnight before eating.
This one brine recipe makes enough for two jars — double it if you're packing all four at once.
components.accommodate: No garlic in this one — safe for your spouse as written.

components.name: Grilled Mexican corn salad
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Grilled Mexican Corn Salad'), adapted
components.why: Elote-style, off the cob. Works as a side for any taco or nacho night — pairs well with the existing Tex-Mex dinners.
ingredients: 2 Tbsp adobo sauce from canned chipotles
steps: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Brush the corn with olive oil and grill, rotating, until kernels are tender and charred in spots, about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and slice the kernels off the cob with a knife.
Toss the kernels with adobo sauce, crumbled cheese, cilantro, lime juice, salt, and pepper.
components.accommodate: Canned chipotles in adobo almost always list garlic in the packing sauce — check the can. If it does, mix your spouse's portion with a pinch of smoked paprika and a little extra lime instead of the adobo sauce.

components.name: Carrot-ginger sauce
components.source: Not from the book — page 287 wasn't photographed, so this is a standard composition, not a transcription. Swap in the book's actual version if you get that page.
components.why: Carrot and ginger blended smooth. This is the sauce that makes the grain bowl taste like a specific dish instead of a pile of roasted vegetables.
steps: Blend everything until completely smooth, adding water as needed to loosen it.
Taste — it should be sweet from the carrot, sharp from the ginger and vinegar.
Thins in the fridge; give it a stir before using.

components.name: Tamari-lime dressing for coconut rice bowls
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Coconut Rice with Brussels Sprouts'), adapted
components.why: Tamari, garlic, lime, and chile — the sauce this whole bowl is built around.
ingredients: 2 Thai chilies, diced, or 0.5 tsp red pepper flakes
steps: Whisk everything together until the sugar dissolves.
Adjust chile to taste — Thai chilies run hot.
components.accommodate: Whisk a small batch without the garlic for your spouse — lime and chile still carry it.

components.name: Creamy broccoli soup
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Creamy Broccoli Soup'), adapted
components.why: Coconut milk instead of cream, so it's vegan and dairy-free while staying genuinely creamy. Garlic sautés with the leek, not raw.
ingredients: 1 large leek, white and light green parts, sliced
1 medium head broccoli, florets and stems
2 cup loosely packed amaranth greens or spinach
steps: Rinse the sliced leek thoroughly in a strainer — grit hides between the layers.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the leek and a few pinches of salt and pepper, stir and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute more. Chop the broccoli, stems and all, into coarse florets and add to the pot. Stir and cook until just softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the white wine vinegar, then add the vegetable broth and coconut milk. Reduce heat to low and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the amaranth greens or spinach, cooking until wilted, about 1 minute.
Let cool slightly, then blend in batches until smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning, adding lemon juice to brighten it up.
components.accommodate: Ladle out 2 cups of the broccoli and broth before the garlic goes in, and finish that portion with a little extra vinegar and lemon for your spouse.

components.name: Spicy cornbread
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Spicy Cornbread'), adapted
components.why: A side that pairs with either soup this week — the red pepper and carrot soup or the broccoli soup.
ingredients: 1 cup spelt flour or all-purpose flour
0.5 cup corn kernels, fresh or frozen
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Stir the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the almond milk, maple syrup, coconut oil, and vinegar until combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined — don't overmix.
Fold in the corn kernels and sliced serrano.
Brush a 10-inch cast-iron skillet with coconut oil. Spread the batter in and bake 20-22 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 15 minutes before serving. Also works in mini skillets (18-20 min) or a 12-cup muffin tin (15-18 min).
components.accommodate: Bake your spouse's portion with a 1:1 GF flour blend instead of spelt or AP flour — same ratios, works fine in a mini skillet on the side of the same bake.

components.name: Basil pesto
components.source: Not from the book — page 275 wasn't photographed, so this is a standard composition, not a transcription. Swap in the book's actual version if you get that page.
components.why: The tartine recipe just says 'any pesto' — this is a straightforward basil version to fill the gap.
steps: Toast the nuts in a dry pan 2-3 minutes until fragrant, then cool slightly.
Blend basil, nuts, garlic, and half the olive oil until mostly smooth.
With the blender running, stream in the rest of the oil. Stir in Parmesan and lemon juice, season with salt.
components.accommodate: Blend a small batch before the garlic goes in for your spouse — lemon and Parmesan carry it fine without.

components.name: Roasted red pepper and carrot soup
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Roasted Red Pepper & Carrot Soup'), adapted
components.why: Fennel sweetens the base the same way it does everywhere else in this collection, layered with real onion and garlic here since it's the household default.
ingredients: 0.25 cup cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion with a pinch of salt and pepper, cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, fennel, carrots, and thyme. Cook, stirring, until the carrot edges begin to brown, 3-4 minutes more.
Stir in balsamic vinegar, roasted red pepper, tomato paste, cannellini beans, and the broth.
Simmer until the carrots are tender, 15-20 minutes.
Cool slightly, then puree in batches in a blender until smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning.
components.accommodate: Ladle out 2 cups of the vegetables and broth right before the garlic goes in, and simmer that portion separately for your spouse — a little extra balsamic and thyme makes up the difference.

components.name: Butternut squash risotto
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Butternut Squash Risotto & Arancini'), adapted
components.why: The book's own move: make this once, eat it as risotto Sunday, then roll the leftovers into arancini a couple nights later.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, season with salt and pepper. Add onion and squash, cook 2-3 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute more. Add the rice, stirring to coat, and cook 1-2 minutes.
Add the wine and cook until absorbed, about 2 minutes.
Add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring continuously and letting each addition absorb before the next — this takes about 20 minutes total, until the rice is tender and creamy.
Stir in butter, Parmesan, and herbs off the heat. Season to taste.
Set aside about half the batch, cooled, in the fridge — that's what becomes arancini.
components.accommodate: Ladle a portion into a small pot before the garlic goes in, and finish it there with a splash of broth and extra Parmesan for your spouse.

components.name: Zucchini tofu ricotta
components.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Zucchini Lasagna with Zucchini Ricotta'), adapted
components.why: Tofu blended with walnuts and lemon reads shockingly close to real ricotta — the book's own promise, and it holds up.
steps: Combine walnuts, garlic, tofu, zucchini, lemon juice, oregano, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper in a food processor.
Process to a spreadable consistency — similar texture to real ricotta.
Fold in the basil by hand at the end so it stays bright rather than pureeing fully green.
components.accommodate: Process a small batch before the garlic goes in for your spouse — lemon and oregano still carry it.

components.name: Pan gravy from turkey drippings
components.source: Mullins Family Cookbook (family site), adapted
components.why: Built straight from the roasted turkey's own drippings — nothing here works without the roast happening first.
steps: Strain the pan drippings through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding the solids. Measure out 2.5 cups.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and thyme, cooking until lightly browned, about 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the drippings. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, whisking constantly, until thickened, 5-10 minutes.
Stir in parsley, season with salt and pepper to taste.
components.accommodate: Use a GF flour blend (1:1) for a small side batch made with a portion of the drippings, for your spouse — same technique, same result.

recipes.title: Breaded {Protein} tacos with tartar sauce
recipes.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Breaded & Baked Artichoke Fish Tacos
steps: In a second bowl, combine panko, hemp seeds, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
{PROTEIN_PREP} Dip each piece in the beaten egg, then press firmly into the panko mixture.
{PROTEIN_PREP} Dip each piece in the flax slurry, then press firmly into the GF panko mixture.
{PROTEIN_COOK} Or air fry at 400°F for 12 minutes, flipping once and spritzing with oil.
Toss the shredded red cabbage with lime juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Ten minutes is enough.
{STARCH_REHEAT} Fill each with tartar sauce, cabbage, protein, thin radish, serrano if you want heat, and cilantro. Lime to finish.
recipes.kid: Breaded and crispy with a dipping sauce is the whole appeal. Skip the serrano and serve the cabbage on the side.
recipes.note: The breading loses its crunch fast. Bread it Sunday, bake it the night you eat it.
recipes.accommodate: Bread your spouse's portion with GF panko and a flax-and-almond-milk slurry instead of egg — whisk 1 Tbsp ground flaxseed into 1/4 cup almond milk, let it thicken 5 minutes, and dip through that instead. Keep it on its own corner of the tray so it doesn't touch the regular breading.

recipes.title: Big pot {Protein} and white beans
steps: Brown the protein in a heavy pot and set aside.
Sweat diced fennel, celery, and carrot in the same fat with salt for 10 minutes — this is your aromatic base in place of onion.
Return the protein, add 3 quarts broth or water, bay, and thyme. Bare simmer 75 minutes.
Add the beans and a big handful of kale; simmer 10 more minutes.
{STARCH_COOK}
Strain and store the cooking liquid separately from the solids. Both of this week's other dinners depend on having them apart.
recipes.kid: Ladle theirs heavy on solids and light on broth, over the starch. Stew sells better than soup.
recipes.note: One pot, three nights. The cooking liquid is the most valuable thing you make.

recipes.title: {Protein} and {starch} bowls
steps: {STARCH_REHEAT}
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Re-crisp the roasted vegetables in the air fryer at 400°F for 6 minutes.
Build bowls: starch, protein, roasted vegetables, pickles, torn lettuce, tomato.
Thin the herb-yogurt with lemon juice until it pours, and spoon it over everything.
recipes.kid: Same components, plated apart instead of piled.
recipes.note: The most flexible weeknight in the system — it takes whatever Sunday produced.

recipes.title: Chimichurri potato salad with {Protein}
recipes.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Chimichurri Potato Salad
steps: If the potatoes aren't already cooked, halve and start them in cold salted water, then simmer 10–14 minutes to fork-tender. Cool to room temperature — dressing hot potatoes makes them fall apart.
Blanch the green beans 2 minutes in boiling water, then straight into ice water to stop the cooking and lock the color. Drain and dry.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Toss potatoes, green beans, and arugula with about three-quarters of the chimichurri, plus salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Add paper-thin radish slices, top with the protein, and finish with the reserved parsley and the last of the chimichurri.
It's better after 20 minutes of sitting. Make it first, eat it last.
recipes.kid: Potatoes and green beans plain on the side, chimichurri as a dip. The red pepper flakes are the sticking point, not the herbs.
recipes.note: Original used three scallions and two garlic cloves. Smoked paprika is doing that work now.

recipes.title: {Protein} chopped salad
steps: {STARCH_REHEAT}
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Chop romaine, cucumber, tomato, and thin apple slices into a big bowl. Add pecans and cranberries.
Re-crisp the roasted vegetables in the air fryer for 6 minutes and add them warm.
Toss with maple-Dijon, top with the protein and crumbled goat cheese. Warm protein over cold salad is the whole idea.
recipes.kid: Deconstruct entirely — protein strips, apple slices, cucumber, dressing to dip.
recipes.note: The temperature contrast is what makes this feel like a meal and not leftovers.

recipes.title: Gem salad with {Protein} and creamy dill
recipes.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Gem Salad with Creamy Dill Dressing
steps: Cube the GF bread with olive oil and flaky salt, bake at 350°F for 12 minutes until crisp. Do this Sunday if you can.

Chop the asparagus into 1-inch pieces and blanch 1–2 minutes until bright green but still with snap. Add the peas for the last 30 seconds, then everything into ice water for a minute. Drain and dry well.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Peel the cucumbers into ribbons and slice the radish paper-thin.
Spread the gem lettuce on a platter with a few spaced dollops of dill dressing underneath — it dresses as people serve themselves instead of wilting the whole thing.
Scatter asparagus, peas, cucumber, radish, avocado, mint, quick pickles, and the protein. Crumble feta over, add croutons last so they stay crisp.
{STARCH_REHEAT}
recipes.kid: Croutons, cucumber ribbons, peas, and feta are the reliable four. Dressing on the side.
recipes.note: Original used a garlic clove in the dressing plus minced chives and pickled red onion. Quick pickles and extra lemon replace all three.

recipes.title: Grilled {Protein} with charred vegetables
steps: {PROTEIN_PREP} Toss with olive oil, oregano, smoked paprika, and a heavy hand of salt.
{STARCH_COOK}
{PROTEIN_COOK}
Corn and zucchini go on the hot side for the last 15 minutes — corn until spotted, zucchini 3 minutes a side.
Cook double what you'll eat tonight. Plate a quarter of it and put the rest straight into containers while you're still standing there.
recipes.kid: Plain starch with butter plus one piece of protein cut into strips, sauce on the side for dipping.
recipes.note: The whole point of Sunday is overshooting. Two-thirds of what comes off the grill is for later in the week.

recipes.title: Grilled romaine Caesar with {Protein}
recipes.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Grilled Romaine Vegan Caesar Wedges
steps: Cube the GF bread, toss with olive oil and salt, and air fry at 375°F for 8 minutes until crisp. Or do this Sunday and store them airtight.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Halve the romaine hearts lengthwise, leaving the core intact so they hold together.
Grill or cast-iron pan on high. Romaine cut-side down for 1–2 minutes until char marks form, then flip for 2 minutes more. Do not walk away — it goes from charred to wilted in about thirty seconds.
Top with dressing, paper-thin radish, croutons, hemp seeds, and the protein. Lemon wedges on the side.
{STARCH_REHEAT}
recipes.kid: Grilled lettuce is a strange sell. Give them raw romaine leaves with dressing to dip, plus croutons and protein.
recipes.note: Original called for chives throughout — the extra capers in the dressing cover that note.

recipes.title: BBQ {Protein} nachos
steps: Warm the black beans with cumin until they thicken.
Spread chips in a single layer on a sheet pan — two thin layers beat one thick pile every time.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT} Scatter it with beans and cheddar over the chips.
Bake at 400°F for 10 minutes until the cheese fully melts.
Top off the heat with avocado, jalapeño, slaw, sour cream, and thinned BBQ sauce.
recipes.kid: Give each kid their own small sheet pan to build. Fifteen minutes of engagement for four minutes of prep.
recipes.note: Check the chips — plain corn is fine, anything labeled nacho or seasoned is not.

recipes.title: Cold {Protein} noodle bowls
steps: {STARCH_REHEAT} Or serve it cold — this bowl works either way.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Slice cucumber thin and leave the snap peas raw.
Loosen the peanut-lime sauce with hot water until it pours.
Build: starch, protein, cucumber, raw snap peas, pickles, lettuce, herbs. Sauce over the top, lime to finish.
recipes.kid: Let them roll it into lettuce cups. Anything they build gets eaten.
recipes.note: No heat required at all if you want it that way. The best 95-degree answer in the system.

recipes.title: {Protein} over GF pasta
steps: Boil GF pasta to two minutes under package time — it goes from firm to mush in about 60 seconds.
Warm the marinara in a wide pan.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT} Lower it into the sauce and simmer 8 minutes.
Toss the drained pasta directly in the sauce with a splash of pasta water and a knob of butter.
Finish with torn mozzarella, Parmesan, and basil.
recipes.kid: The safest meal in the system. Butter and Parmesan on the side if the sauce is contentious.
recipes.note: Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining. It's what makes the sauce cling.

recipes.title: Roast {Protein} over root vegetables
steps: {PROTEIN_PREP} Rub with softened butter, thyme, and pepper.
{PROTEIN_COOK}
Roast the root vegetables and squash at 425°F for 35 minutes, cut-side down for the deepest caramelization.
{STARCH_COOK}
Toss the roasted vegetables with maple-Dijon and pecans while still warm — warm vegetables absorb dressing, cold ones don't.
If you roasted poultry, the carcass goes into the broth pot tonight, not tomorrow.
recipes.kid: Squash rings look like scalloped moons and go down easier than you'd guess.
recipes.note: The highest-yield hour in the rotation. One oven, two racks, three nights of food.

recipes.title: Sheet pan {Protein} with roasted roots
steps: Cut the roots to a uniform size across two sheet pans. Oil, salt, thyme, 425°F for 45 minutes.
Whisk maple syrup, Dijon, vinegar, salt, and pepper into a glaze.
{PROTEIN_PREP} Brush with half the glaze.
{PROTEIN_COOK}
{STARCH_COOK}
The shortest Sunday in the rotation and it still yields three nights.
recipes.kid: Maple glaze buys a lot of goodwill on fish. Roasted parsnip is sweet enough to pass as a carrot.
recipes.note: Under 95 minutes start to finish. The one to pick on a busy Sunday.

recipes.title: Smoked and pulled {Protein}
steps: Coat generously with smoked paprika, cumin, brown sugar, salt, and pepper.
Smoker at 250°F with hickory or cherry.
{PROTEIN_COOK} For poultry, go all the way to about 195°F so the collagen breaks down and it pulls apart.
{STARCH_COOK}
Pull with two forks. Sauce only half — plain pulled protein is far more versatile later in the week.
recipes.kid: Serve the unsauced half with cheese melted over it, sauce on the side.
recipes.note: Sauce half, leave half plain. This is the single highest-leverage decision in the whole week.

recipes.title: {Protein} and {starch} soup
steps: Bring 2 quarts of Sunday's broth to a simmer with sliced carrot and celery. Cook 8 minutes.
Brown the mushrooms hard in butter in a separate pan for 6 minutes, then add — that browning is where the depth comes from.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT} Add it and the cooked starch to the pot and warm through.
Whisk 3 eggs with the juice of 2 lemons. Ladle in a cup of hot broth while whisking hard to temper, then stir back into the pot off the heat.
Finish with parsley and more lemon than feels right. Don't let it boil after the eggs go in.
recipes.kid: Ladle theirs before the egg-lemon step — it's chicken and rice soup at that point.
recipes.note: This is the night that justifies simmering broth on Sunday.

recipes.title: Squash soup with crispy {Protein}
recipes.source: Love & Lemons (Jeanine Donofrio), adapted, Sheet Pan Squash Soup
steps: Warm the squash soup gently on the stove. It thickens hard in the fridge — thin with broth or water until it pours.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
{STARCH_REHEAT}
Ladle the soup and top with the crispy protein, a swirl of coconut milk, toasted pepitas, and a drizzle of chimichurri.
The chimichurri is what turns this from a side soup into dinner — don't skip it.
recipes.kid: Blend theirs extra smooth and serve with the starch on the side to dunk. Toppings in small bowls so they choose.
recipes.note: Soup was made entirely on Sunday. Tonight is warming and topping, nothing more.

recipes.title: {Protein}-stuffed sweet potatoes
steps: {STARCH_REHEAT}
Split them open, fluff the insides with a fork, add butter and salt before anything else goes on.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT} Toss it with warm BBQ sauce.
Pile it in, top with cheddar, and run under the broiler or air fryer at 375°F for 4 minutes.
Finish with slaw right on top, sour cream, and cilantro.
recipes.kid: Slaw on top is optional. Cheese is not.
recipes.note: Bake the potatoes Sunday alongside everything else and this becomes a 10-minute night.

recipes.title: {Protein} tacos
steps: {STARCH_REHEAT}
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Dress half the slaw with lime and salt — 10 minutes is all it needs.
Mash the avocado with lime and salt.
Build: starch, protein, slaw, salsa verde, avocado, cotija, hard squeeze of lime.
recipes.kid: Deconstruct it. Same food in separate piles, zero negotiation.
recipes.note: Pure assembly. Nothing here is actually cooked tonight.

recipes.title: Lemon coconut date balls
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, title unconfirmed), adapted — spot-check quantities against the book
steps: Add the base and this flavor's ingredients to a food processor together.
Pulse until the mixture sticks together when pinched — if it's too crumbly, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Roll into balls. Roll in a mix of 0.33 cup shredded coconut and 0.5 tsp lemon zest.
Store at room temperature up to two weeks.
recipes.kid: This whole category is built for lunchboxes — no cooking, no allergens beyond nuts, and kids can help roll them.
recipes.note: role:snack means the weekly roll never picks this automatically. Make a batch whenever the freezer's low.

recipes.title: PB&J date balls
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, title unconfirmed), adapted — spot-check quantities against the book
steps: Add the base and this flavor's ingredients to a food processor together.
Pulse until the mixture sticks together when pinched — if it's too crumbly, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Roll into balls. Roll in 0.5 cup crushed freeze-dried strawberries.
Store at room temperature up to two weeks.
recipes.kid: This whole category is built for lunchboxes — no cooking, no allergens beyond nuts, and kids can help roll them.
recipes.note: role:snack means the weekly roll never picks this automatically. Make a batch whenever the freezer's low.

recipes.title: Carrot granola date balls
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, title unconfirmed), adapted — spot-check quantities against the book
steps: Add the base and this flavor's ingredients to a food processor together.
Pulse until the mixture sticks together when pinched — if it's too crumbly, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Roll into balls. No roll-in for this one — leave it plain after shaping.
Store at room temperature up to two weeks.
recipes.kid: This whole category is built for lunchboxes — no cooking, no allergens beyond nuts, and kids can help roll them.
recipes.note: role:snack means the weekly roll never picks this automatically. Make a batch whenever the freezer's low.

recipes.title: Matcha pistachio date balls
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, title unconfirmed), adapted — spot-check quantities against the book
steps: Add the base and this flavor's ingredients to a food processor together.
Pulse until the mixture sticks together when pinched — if it's too crumbly, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Roll into balls. Roll in a mix of 0.33 cup crushed pistachios and 0.25 tsp matcha powder.
Store at room temperature up to two weeks.
recipes.kid: This whole category is built for lunchboxes — no cooking, no allergens beyond nuts, and kids can help roll them.
recipes.note: role:snack means the weekly roll never picks this automatically. Make a batch whenever the freezer's low.

recipes.title: Tahini spice date balls
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, title unconfirmed), adapted — spot-check quantities against the book
steps: Add the base and this flavor's ingredients to a food processor together.
Pulse until the mixture sticks together when pinched — if it's too crumbly, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Roll into balls. Roll in 0.33 cup sesame seeds.
Store at room temperature up to two weeks.
recipes.kid: This whole category is built for lunchboxes — no cooking, no allergens beyond nuts, and kids can help roll them.
recipes.note: role:snack means the weekly roll never picks this automatically. Make a batch whenever the freezer's low.

recipes.title: Cookie dough date balls
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, title unconfirmed), adapted — spot-check quantities against the book
steps: Add the base and this flavor's ingredients to a food processor together.
Pulse until the mixture sticks together when pinched — if it's too crumbly, add water a teaspoon at a time.
Roll into balls. Fold in 0.5 cup chocolate chips — stir these in by hand at the end, don't process them.
Store at room temperature up to two weeks.
recipes.kid: This whole category is built for lunchboxes — no cooking, no allergens beyond nuts, and kids can help roll them.
recipes.note: role:snack means the weekly roll never picks this automatically. Make a batch whenever the freezer's low.

recipes.title: Sweet potato wedges with herbed farro and tahini
ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato, cut into 12 wedges
steps: Toss the sweet potato wedges with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a parchment-lined sheet pan, spread with a little space between pieces.
Roast at 425°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown at the edges.
{STARCH_COOK}
In a large bowl, toss the cooked farro with olive oil, salt, lemon juice, parsley, cilantro, chives, arugula, and a pinch of cayenne.
Arrange the herbed farro on a platter, top with the roasted sweet potato wedges, and drizzle with tahini dressing. Serve with lemon wedges and red pepper flakes if you want more heat.
recipes.kid: Sweet potato wedges alone are the win here. Give them the wedges plain with the dressing on the side and skip the arugula.
recipes.accommodate: Toss your spouse's portion of farro salad before the chives go in — parsley and lemon carry it fine without.

recipes.title: Summer thyme pasta
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Five Easy Favorites' pasta spread), adapted and doubled to serve 4
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over low heat. Add shallot and cook gently until soft.
Add cherry tomatoes and thyme sprigs, a pinch of salt and red pepper flakes. Cook until the tomatoes start bursting, about 6 minutes, then add garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Stir in balsamic vinegar and cooked orecchiette. Toss with a splash of pasta water until it comes together.
Top with shaved pecorino and fresh basil.
recipes.kid: Plain buttered pasta with a spoon of pecorino on the side covers most of these if the vegetable mix is a hard sell that night.
recipes.accommodate: Cook your spouse's portion of tomatoes and thyme without the shallot and garlic — pull it aside right after the tomatoes burst, before those go in.

recipes.title: Zucchini carbonara
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Five Easy Favorites' pasta spread), adapted and doubled to serve 4
steps: Whisk the eggs with almond milk and grated pecorino in a small bowl.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add zucchini strips with a pinch of salt and pepper, sauté until soft, about 6 minutes.
Remove from heat, add the cooked bucatini, then pour in the egg mixture and toss immediately — the residual heat cooks the egg into a sauce without scrambling it.
Top with fresh basil.
recipes.kid: Plain buttered pasta with a spoon of pecorino on the side covers most of these if the vegetable mix is a hard sell that night.
recipes.accommodate: Boil a small separate pot of GF bucatini or spaghetti for your spouse — regular and GF pasta shouldn't share water.

recipes.title: Lemon aglio olio with kale
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Five Easy Favorites' pasta spread), adapted and doubled to serve 4
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over low heat. Add garlic and red pepper flakes, cook until fragrant, about 1 minute — don't let the garlic brown.
Add kale in batches with a pinch of salt, cooking until wilted, about 6 minutes.
Add the cooked spaghetti and lemon zest, tossing with a little pasta water until it comes together.
Top with toasted pine nuts and shaved pecorino.
recipes.kid: Plain buttered pasta with a spoon of pecorino on the side covers most of these if the vegetable mix is a hard sell that night.
recipes.accommodate: Sauté your spouse's portion of kale in its own small pan without garlic — red pepper flakes and lemon zest carry it fine alone.

recipes.title: Fennel fettuccine
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Five Easy Favorites' pasta spread), adapted and doubled to serve 4
steps: Slice the fennel bulbs into wedges and roast or sauté until tender.
Mix the caesar dressing with the reserved pasta cooking water until smooth and pourable.
Toss the cooked fettuccine with the fennel, peas, chopped chives, tarragon, and the dressing.
Serve with lemon wedges.
recipes.kid: Plain buttered pasta with a spoon of pecorino on the side covers most of these if the vegetable mix is a hard sell that night.
recipes.accommodate: Toss your spouse's portion before the chives go in, and use the caesar dressing's garlic-free batch (see that component) — tarragon and lemon fill the gap.

recipes.title: Roasted cauliflower pasta with yogurt and harissa
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Five Easy Favorites' pasta spread), adapted and doubled to serve 4
steps: Roast the cauliflower florets at 425°F with olive oil and salt for 25 minutes until charred at the edges.
Toss the cooked pasta with roasted cauliflower, harissa, and Greek yogurt until everything is coated.
Top with roasted chickpeas, fresh mint, and arugula or microgreens.
recipes.kid: Plain buttered pasta with a spoon of pecorino on the side covers most of these if the vegetable mix is a hard sell that night.
recipes.accommodate: No allium or red meat here — the only accommodation is pasta shape if gluten is the concern for a given night; swap in GF pasta same as any other night.

recipes.title: Kale and sweet potato lasagna roll-ups
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Kale & Sweet Potato Lasagna Roll-Ups'), adapted
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato, cut into small cubes
steps: Toss the sweet potato cubes with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a parchment-lined sheet pan. Roast at 425°F for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
Steam the kale leaves 1 minute until just wilted, then squeeze the excess water out on a kitchen towel.
{STARCH_COOK} Toss the cooked noodles with a little olive oil so they don't stick together while you work.
Spread a cup of marinara across the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish.

Lay each noodle flat, spread 3-4 tablespoons of ricotta down the middle, then a piece of kale, sweet potato cubes, a pinch of sage, and red pepper flakes. Roll each one up and place seam-side down in the dish.
Spoon the remaining marinara over the top, cover, and bake at 425°F for 20 minutes.
This makes 12 rolls — three per adult tonight, the rest for two more nights.
recipes.kid: Unroll theirs into an open-face version — noodle on the bottom, everything else on top, easier to eat and just as good.
recipes.accommodate: Boil 2-3 GF lasagna noodles in a separate small pot for your spouse's rolls — they turn to mush fast if boiled together with regular noodles.

recipes.title: Sunshine sweet potato curry
steps: In a pot, warm coconut oil and sauté the onion until soft, about 6 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Add cardamom seeds, coriander, and cumin, toasting 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in ginger, turmeric, and cayenne.
Add coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes to let the spices bloom. Stir in lime zest and vinegar. This is the curry base.
Add the sweet potato and cauliflower, simmer 12-15 minutes until just tender. Add the bell pepper and jalapeño for the last 5 minutes.
{PROTEIN_COOK} Fold it in along with the spinach, cooking just until wilted.
{STARCH_COOK} Serve the curry over rice with lime juice, cilantro, and crushed cashews.
recipes.kid: Curry flavor is a coin flip at this age. Serve a plain portion of rice, cauliflower, and sweet potato on the side before the sauce goes on, with yogurt to cool it down.
recipes.accommodate: Simmer your spouse's curry base before the onion and garlic go in — bloom the spices in coconut oil directly, then coconut milk and spices as normal. It's a slightly flatter base; extra ginger and lime make up the difference.

recipes.title: Carrot-ginger grain bowl with tofu
ingredients: 10 small heirloom carrots, cut into cubes
steps: Peel 3 of the carrots into ribbons with a vegetable peeler and set aside for the salad; cube the rest.
{PROTEIN_PREP} Toss the cubed protein and cubed carrots separately with oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan.
{PROTEIN_COOK} Roast the carrots alongside at 400°F for 15-17 minutes until browned at the edges but still with some bite.
{STARCH_COOK}
Toss the greens with the cooked millet, carrot ribbons, and almonds.
Assemble the bowls with the salad, roasted carrots, protein, and avocado. Serve with carrot-ginger sauce on the side.
recipes.kid: Deconstruct it — millet, plain roasted carrots, avocado, and protein in separate piles, sauce for dipping.
recipes.note: The book's ingredient list didn't include a protein — the photo shows what looks like tofu, but I didn't fabricate a quantity for it. I added a protein slot defaulting to tofu since a family dinner needs one; adjust the default if you'd rather it default to something else.

recipes.title: Coconut rice with charred Brussels sprouts
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Coconut Rice with Brussels Sprouts'), adapted
steps: Cook the rice using coconut milk in place of some of the water, per package ratio. Fluff with a fork and keep warm.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the halved Brussels sprouts cut-side down and sear undisturbed 2-3 minutes until deeply browned. Toss and continue cooking 7-10 minutes until tender.
Add the scallions during the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Serve the rice in bowls with the Brussels sprouts, basil, avocado, and sesame seeds. Drizzle with the sauce and sriracha, lime on the side.
recipes.kid: Plain rice with a little of the coconut milk and some avocado usually works even when the sprouts don't.
recipes.note: As printed this is a vegetarian side/light dinner — no protein was in the book's ingredient list, despite what the plated photo suggests. Pair it with a simply grilled protein on the side if you want it heartier, or leave it as written.

recipes.title: Creamy broccoli soup with crispy {Protein}
steps: Warm the broccoli soup gently on the stove — it thickens in the fridge, thin with a splash of broth if needed.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Ladle into bowls and top with the crispy protein, a swirl of coconut milk, and red pepper flakes.
recipes.kid: Blend theirs extra smooth and skip the red pepper flakes. Serve with something to dip — GF crackers or toast.
recipes.note: Soup was made entirely on Sunday. Tonight is warming and topping.

recipes.title: Avocado pesto mozzarella tartines
steps: Drizzle the bread with olive oil and toast in a toaster or on a grill.
Heat a thin layer of olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the sage leaves and fry lightly without browning, 10-15 seconds a side. Drain on a paper towel.
Top each piece of toast with mozzarella, avocado, watercress, thyme, and fried sage. Dollop with pesto.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve extra pesto on the side.
recipes.kid: Skip the watercress and sage for theirs — bread, mozzarella, avocado, and a small dollop of pesto covers most of what they'll eat here.
recipes.accommodate: The book's own gluten-free note applies directly: use GF bread for your spouse's slices, same everything else.

recipes.title: Red pepper carrot soup with garlic croutons and {Protein}
steps: Toss the bread cubes with a drizzle of olive oil and the minced garlic on a baking sheet. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake at 350°F for 10-15 minutes until crispy.
Warm the soup on the stove.
{PROTEIN_REHEAT}
Serve bowls with a drizzle of olive oil, the protein, and croutons on top.
recipes.kid: Croutons are the whole sell here. Give them extra on the side even if the soup itself is a hard pass.
recipes.accommodate: Make your spouse's croutons in a separate small batch without the garlic clove — plain olive oil and salt still crisps up fine.

recipes.title: Butternut squash risotto
steps: Ladle the risotto into bowls right off the stove — it doesn't hold well, so serve it the moment it's done.
Top with extra herbs and Parmesan.
Set aside roughly half the batch, cooled, before anyone goes back for seconds — that's arancini night.
recipes.kid: Risotto is basically fancy rice and cheese as far as they're concerned. Serve it slightly cooler than you'd like it — kids tend to want it less molten than a risotto normally comes off the stove.
recipes.note: The book's printed quantities are written to feed 4 with leftovers for arancini already built in. If your crew tends to finish the pot, double the batch.

recipes.title: Squash arancini with marinara
ingredients: 2 oz smoked mozzarella, cut into 12 small cubes (optional)
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Spread the panko on a plate. Scoop a heaping tablespoon of the leftover risotto and roll it into a 2-inch ball.
If using, press a cube of smoked mozzarella into the center of each ball and re-seal it around the cheese.
Roll each ball in the panko to coat, then place on the baking sheet.
Bake 25 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Warm the marinara and serve alongside for dipping.
recipes.kid: Fried rice balls with a dipping sauce is about as close to a guaranteed win as this whole collection gets.
recipes.accommodate: Roll your spouse's balls in GF panko instead — the book's own gluten-free note for this recipe. Keep them on their own corner of the tray.

recipes.title: Zucchini lasagna with tofu ricotta
recipes.source: Cookbook (photographed, 'Zucchini Lasagna with Zucchini Ricotta'), adapted
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the lasagna noodles per package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse.
Drizzle a 9x13-inch pan with olive oil. Layer: a third of the noodles, half the tofu ricotta, half the diced tomatoes.
Layer more zucchini planks over that, then add the remaining tomatoes.
Repeat with the remaining noodles, ricotta, and zucchini, finishing with a layer of zucchini planks on top.
Top with grated pecorino, or skip it to keep it fully vegan. Drizzle with olive oil.
Bake, covered, 20-30 minutes, or until the zucchini is tender but still has a bite and the tomatoes are bubbling. Uncover and bake 10 more minutes.
Let rest 15 minutes before serving. Season with fresh cracked black pepper.
recipes.kid: The tofu genuinely doesn't read as tofu once it's blended and baked — most kids treat this like a regular vegetable lasagna.
recipes.accommodate: The lasagna noodles here are already brown rice — no gluten workaround needed beyond the tofu ricotta's own note about the garlic.

recipes.title: Cast iron chicken
steps: Turn on the range fan — this sears hot enough to smoke a little.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
Season the chicken generously with salt and pepper. Sear skin-side down in a hot cast-iron pan with oil, 4 minutes per side.
Transfer the pan to the oven and finish 16 minutes, until the thickest part reads 165°F.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
recipes.kid: Slice it thin off the bone — plain seared chicken is one of the least controversial proteins in the house.
recipes.note: The book's version doesn't specify a quantity — this assumes 4 bone-in breasts for the family. Adjust sear time down if using boneless.

recipes.title: Beer can smoked chicken
steps: Mix the rub: paprika, chili powder, thyme, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, salt, and black pepper. This makes enough for two chickens.
Coat both chickens generously with the rub, including under the skin if you can get a hand in there.
Open the beer cans and set each chicken upright on top of one, using it as a stand in the smoker.
Fire up the smoker to 275°F. Cook about 90 minutes, or until the thickest part of the breast reads 165°F.
Carve one chicken for tonight. Strip the second — breast sliced, dark meat pulled — for weeknight bowls, tacos, or soup.
recipes.kid: Plain sliced breast meat off either bird. The rub has a little cayenne — scrape it off their portion if the color alone is a tell.
recipes.accommodate: Rub a third smaller portion of thighs with a version of this mix made without garlic and onion powder — smoked paprika and thyme still carry it for your spouse.

recipes.title: Oven baked chicken wings
steps: The night before: toss the wings with baking powder and salt, then refrigerate uncovered overnight — this is what gets the skin crackling crisp without frying.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack on top, sprayed with nonstick spray.
Pat the wings dry and arrange skin-side up in a single layer on the rack.
Bake, turning every 20 minutes, until crispy and browned — 45 minutes to an hour depending on wing size.
For the rosemary dry rub version: toss cooked wings with salt, garlic powder, cayenne, baking powder, and chopped rosemary before serving.
For the hot sauce version: melt butter with Frank's hot sauce, toss wings in it, and serve with ranch dressing on the side.
recipes.kid: Plain wings, sauce on the side for dipping rather than tossed.
recipes.accommodate: Toss a portion without garlic powder for your spouse if going the rosemary route — rosemary and cayenne still carry it. The hot sauce version has no allium at all.
recipes.note: This one is a standalone dinner night, not a leftover-generating Sunday anchor — pair with a starch and vegetable side and eat it all in one sitting. Needs the overnight fridge step, so start the dry brine the night before.

recipes.title: Turkey zucchini meatballs with lemon-garlic yogurt
steps: Make the sauce first: stir together cream, yogurt, lemon zest and juice, crushed garlic, olive oil, sumac, salt, and pepper. Chill while you make the meatballs.
Squeeze the grated zucchini in a towel to get rid of excess water — skip this and the meatballs won't hold together.
Combine the turkey, zucchini, green onion, egg, mint, cilantro, garlic, cumin, salt, pepper, and cayenne in a large bowl. Mix with your hands and shape into small patties.
Pan-sear over medium-high heat until browned and cooked through, about 4 minutes a side.
Serve with the sauce for dipping.
recipes.kid: Skip the sauce for theirs, or serve it on the side — the sumac has a sharp, unfamiliar tang that's a bigger sell than the meatballs themselves.
recipes.accommodate: Leave the garlic and green onion out of a quarter of the meatball mix and skip the garlic in a small side portion of sauce, for your spouse — mint, cilantro, and cumin still carry the meatballs, and lemon carries the sauce.

recipes.title: Turkey basil meatballs with burrata
steps: Combine turkey, egg, basil, Dijon, black pepper, Italian seasoning, cumin, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, salt, cayenne, and panko in a large bowl. Roll into 16 golf-ball-sized meatballs.
Brown the edges in a large skillet over medium-high heat with a little olive oil, about 5 minutes — they don't need to cook through yet.
Reduce to medium-low, add the marinara, cover, and cook 10 more minutes.
Nestle the burrata into the sauce in clumps and let it sit as whole 'cheese balls' rather than stirring it in. Cook 5 more minutes.
Serve over pasta, spaghetti squash, or with garlic bread.
recipes.kid: Meatballs and cheese-forward sauce is about as close to a guaranteed win as this whole rotation gets. Skip the red pepper flakes on their portion if you're making it milder overall.
recipes.accommodate: Regular panko — swap in GF panko for a portion made separately for your spouse. Garlic powder is light here; leave it out of a quarter of the mix if it matters, basil and Italian seasoning still carry it.

recipes.title: Ginger glazed sea bass
recipes.source: Mullins Family Cookbook (family site), adapted and doubled to serve 4
steps: Stir together honey, soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, ginger, garlic, and olive oil in a shallow dish.
Season the fillets with salt and pepper and place in the marinade, skin-side down if applicable. Cover and refrigerate 20 minutes.
{STARCH_COOK}
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Remove the fish, reserving the marinade, and fry 4-6 minutes a side, turning once, until it flakes easily.
Pour the reserved marinade into the skillet and reduce over medium heat until it's glaze-thick, a couple minutes.
Spoon the glaze over the fish and serve over rice.
recipes.kid: Sea bass is mild and flaky — a good one to introduce without much resistance. Go light on the glaze for their piece since the marinade skews savory.
recipes.accommodate: Marinate a portion without garlic — ginger and honey still do most of the work. Use tamari in place of soy sauce for that portion too, same ratio, since it's already the gluten swap for this pantry.

recipes.title: Roasted turkey breast with herb butter
steps: Let the turkey stand at room temperature 30 minutes before cooking.
Preheat oven to 325°F. Lightly oil a baking dish and spread the lemon slices across the bottom.
Combine the softened butter with garlic, thyme, sage, and rosemary.
Dry the turkey thoroughly. Loosen the skin from the breast meat with your fingers and spread half the herb butter underneath. Secure the skin with toothpicks if needed.
Set the turkey breast-side up on the lemon slices. Spread the remaining butter over the top and season with salt and pepper.
Roast until the thickest part reads 165°F, about 90 minutes. Reserve the pan drippings for gravy.
Let stand 20 minutes before carving.
recipes.kid: Plain sliced turkey with gravy poured tableside rather than over the whole plate — some kids are particular about sauce touching everything.
recipes.accommodate: Spread a garlic-free version of the herb butter under a portion of the skin for your spouse — thyme, sage, and rosemary carry it fine without.
recipes.note: This one pairs naturally with several weeknights already in the rotation that accept turkey as a protein — bowls, soup, pasta, nachos, and stuffed sweet potatoes will all pull it in if there's turkey left over.
